testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A device that warns when air pressure is low.
A tube that sends air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that warns when air pressure is low.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a low pressure warning device. A wig wag is one type of warning device. When air pressure drops between 55 and 75 psi, it drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view.

questions.question: Which braking system uses the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: The service brake system activates when you press the brake pedal while driving. It applies and releases the brakes for normal driving.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: A single system with two sets of controls.
One system for each side of the truck.
Two separate systems that share one set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate systems that share one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems controlled by a single brake control. One system usually brakes the rear axle. The other system brakes the front axle.

questions.question: What does it mean if the safety relief valve is releasing air?

options.text: This is normal and nothing to worry about.
Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air only if pressure gets too high. If it starts releasing air, there is a problem. Have a mechanic repair it right away.

questions.question: How must an emergency brake be controlled?
questions.explanation: All trucks and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. Since air pressure can leak away, these brakes must be held by mechanical force.

questions.question: What color light warns that an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working?
questions.explanation: ABS warning lights are usually yellow. If the ABS is not working, the regular brakes will still work.

questions.question: What type of air brake system do most heavy-duty vehicles use?
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems. These have two separate braking systems controlled by one brake control. Each system brakes different axles.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage allowed in a static leakage test for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a triple combination vehicle, air should not leak more than 5 psi in one minute. If it leaks faster, something needs repair and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times.
Push in the brake control knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob.
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a yellow diamond-shaped knob. Pull it out to set the parking brake. Push it in to release it.

questions.question: What can happen if you do not drain the air tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air collects in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and compressor oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, you must wait for the air compressor to build up at least ____ in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too often can:

options.text: Release air faster than the compressor can replace it.
Add more air to the braking system.
Make the brake pedal more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too often can release air from the system faster than the compressor can replace it.

questions.question: The air leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes should not exceed ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a single vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should not exceed 2 psi in one minute. If the leakage rate is higher, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: The application pressure gauge shows:

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
The temperature of air in the braking system.
The pressure of air coming from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. Not all vehicles with air brakes have this gauge.

questions.question: ABS brakes:

options.text: Help prevent your wheels from locking up.
Prevent your vehicle from accelerating when going uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help prevent your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) brakes prevent your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator in an air brake system:

options.text: Prevents ice from forming in the braking system.
Lubricates parts of the braking system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents ice from forming in the braking system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems include an evaporator that adds alcohol to the system. The alcohol helps prevent ice from forming inside the system.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most heavy-duty vehicles have?
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles are equipped with dual air brake systems for safety.

questions.question: What shows you how much pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.explanation: The supply pressure gauge tells you how much air pressure is in each of your vehicle's air tanks. All air brake vehicles must have this gauge.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are activated, you should never:

options.text: Release air from the air storage tanks.
Open the door to the cab.

questions.explanation: Never apply the brake pedal if your spring brakes are activated. The brakes can be damaged if they receive both spring pressure and air pressure at the same time.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle is:
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle, the maximum air leakage rate during an applied leakage test is 4 psi in a minute.

questions.question: At what air pressure level does an air compressor governor stop pumping air into the tanks?
questions.explanation: An air compressor governor stops pumping when the air tanks reach 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times
Push in the brake control knob

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: The parking brake in air brake vehicles is controlled by a knob on the dashboard. Pull the knob out to apply the brakes. Push it in to release them.

questions.question: What is the purpose of anti-lock brakes?

options.text: Prevent the wheels from locking up
Stop the vehicle from speeding uphill
Stop the vehicle from speeding downhill

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes (ABS) prevent the wheels from locking up when the driver brakes hard.

questions.question: Brake linings should be:
questions.explanation: Brake linings must be free of oil and grease. They should not be loose or too thin.

questions.question: What can a modulating control valve control?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets the driver gradually apply spring brakes. It is controlled by a lever on the dashboard in equipped vehicles.
